parsed_response.reasoning: The claim of a compile failure is false under TypeScript structural typing: a method with fewer parameters (e.g. LarkCalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent) and Office365CalendarService.createEvent(event), both shown updated in the diff) is assignable to an interface method requiring an extra parameter, so these classes still satisfy Calendar. The diff also shows the non-Google services were consciously adapted to the new array shape (e.g. `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`), while Google uniquely uses credentialId because only its service writes to multiple per-credential calendars (`cal.credentialId === credentialId`). The 'silently ignore credentialId' behavior is the intended fallback, not a defect, so the finding's described defect does not exist.

judged_text: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId: number), but only GoogleCalendarService was updated — LarkCalendarService.createEvent(event), Office365CalendarService.createEvent(event), and BaseCalendarService still declare/accept a single-event signature. Every other Calendar implementer no longer satisfies the interface (compile failure in any typechecked consumer of Calendar), and CalendarManager.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id) passes a second argument these services silently ignore — the credentialId parameter reaches only Google, so any per-credential behavior indexed off it diverges by provider.

adjudication.rationale: The diff updates the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts), and CalendarManager now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts). GoogleCalendarService was updated to accept the second arg, but other implementers shown still declare `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` (e.g., packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts and packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, both `implements Calendar`). That is a concrete interface/implementation mismatch that will fail typechecking for those classes and/or for the `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` call when the concrete type is one of those providers.
